problem:
Consider the line $y=4x+5$ and linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ -1 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the equation of the image of the line under the action of $T?$

feedback.problem:
Consider the line $y=x+3$ and linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the equation of the image of the line under the action of $T?$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, notice that the line $y=x+3$ passes through the points $C(0,3)$ and $L(1,4)$ since the coordinates of both points satisfy the equation.

To find the image of $C$ and $L$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the points:

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 \\ 3 & 5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective image points are ${C}^{′}(-3,3)$ and ${L}^{′}(0,5).$

Finally, we write the equation of the line that passes through ${C}^{′}$ and ${L}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-3 & =\frac{5-3}{0-(-3)}(x-(-3)) \\ y-3 & =\frac{2}{3}(x+3) \\ 3y-9 & =2x+6 \\ 2x-3y+15 & =0\end{aligned}
$$
